### Hands on workshops


Hands on workshops are a great way to pick up spatial analysis skills in a communal environment, with access to a pre-prepared analysis environment and dataset, with ability to talk to the trainers who are working in this field.

Such workshops are regularly delivered for the Australian research community through a few different avenues. Check these links for upcoming sessions:

* [**Biocommons Workshops**](https://www.biocommons.org.au/webinars-workshops): Australia-wide, covering a wide array of bioinformatics analyses, including spatial transcriptomics. Past webinars are also [available online](https://www.biocommons.org.au/past-events). These workshops are often very popular and can fill up, so registration is essential!
* [**QCIF Digitial Research workshops**](https://www.qcif.edu.au/training-calendar): QCIF offers a regular calendar of bioinformatics, statistics, AI and programming workshops. Spatial transcriptomics and single cell transcriptomics are in the rotation. These are free for those at QCIF member organisations, others may attend for a small fee. Registration again essential!



### Self Directed learning

Many of these workshops share their material only and can be used directly - a recommended selection of online material is described in the [tutorials section](g_tutorials.html)


### Direct Support

Much of this material has been developed at QCIF Digital research via support and funding from the [Australian Biocommons workflow commons program](https://www.biocommons.org.au/workflow-commons). 




QCIF Digital research can provide provide you with further supports in several ways. These services are available to all, but are subsidised for QCIF's member organisations - you can check if you're at one of the [member organisations here](https://www.qcif.edu.au/form). As of 2026 that' includes; QUT, GU, JCU, CQU, UniSC, SCU, Bond and Malaghan

* [**Free Consultation Support:**](https://www.qcif.edu.au/form) Researchers and PhD students at our member universities have access to some (fully subsidised!) consultation support. If you have a question about your research at any stage of the process, get in touch!
 Go to the [form](https://www.qcif.edu.au/form) and request _'Member's support'_
* [**Project work:**](https://www.qcif.edu.au/form) Project analysis: QCIF staff can work on a fee-for-service model, usually provided as a fractional FTE contribution over a period of time. [Enquire here](https://www.qcif.edu.au/form)
* [**Bioinformatics Accelerator:**](https://www.qcif.edu.au/products/bioinformatics-accelerator) Additionally QCIF provides the [Bioinformatics accelerator](https://www.qcif.edu.au/products/bioinformatics-accelerator) program - one-on-one project guidance and expert advice for PhD students and researchers who are picking up a new bioinformatics analysis skillset, including spatial and single cell analyses! Partly subsidised for member universities and organisations; [program details here](https://www.qcif.edu.au/products/bioinformatics-accelerator), [apply here](https://comms3528.wixforms.com/f/7480822400074908698) .
* [**Grant application support**](https://www.qcif.edu.au/form)



Extensive collaboration from the University of Sydney's Sydney Informatics Hub (SIH) has also enabled training - material development and delivery, and streamlined compute environments via bioshell.

* [Bioshell project](https://sydney-informatics-hub.github.io/BioShell-User-Guide/index): Compute environments for training and bioinformatics analysis.
* [Get in touch with SIH here](https://www.sydney.edu.au/research/facilities/sydney-informatics-hub.html)
